**Finding submitted: ASSIGN — deviation (preferred-level cure).**

**What I found**
- **Section 10.2(a) (p0406)** is the operative assignment clause. It requires consent from the Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee, Certificateholders and 66-2/3% Controlling Class Noteholders — but *not* from the Issuer or Depositor, so our side holds no consent right over a Servicer assignment, the standard is unqualified, and there is no competitor bar.
- **Section 7.6 (p0348)** is expressly carved out of 10.2(a), letting Cellco assign the Agreement to any Cellco Affiliate with no consent and no notice — this defeats both the preferred "Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent" element and the fallback rule that every non-successor assignment needs consent.
- **Already satisfied, so untouched:** Section 5.3 (p0249) gives the Depositor consent-free merger/succession/Affiliate assignment rights; Section 7.1 (p0314) bars Servicer resignation except on legal inability, so a change of control on our side gives Cellco no exit.

**The redline (validated, ok:true)** makes two surgical changes only: it drops Section 7.6 from the 10.2(a) exception list and adds the Issuer's consent, not unreasonably withheld, for Servicer assignments; and it inserts one sentence barring assignment to a competitor of the Issuer or Depositor. Section 5.3 and the Section 7.4 successor-servicer mechanics are preserved, so nothing on our outbound leg is weakened. Section 6.4 delegation was reviewed and not flagged — delegation does not relieve Cellco of responsibility.
